Emily — great questions. Attached is a concise proposal + cost workbook, and below are three pragmatic reservation bundles aligned to your May 15 production target. We’ve annotated ramp timing, min GPUs (reserved floor), burst strategy, and expected steady-state throughput for each.

High-level assumptions (please confirm):
- Model: 70B decoder (8k context) — memory ~40GB/model instance at fp16 (we can quantize to int8 if you want to reduce memory footprint)
- Target 95th pct tail latency: <350ms for interactive flows
- Region: us-east-1

Options (summary):
1) Starter — "Baseline"
   - Reserved: 8 x A100-40GB (min 8 GPUs reserved)
   - Initial config: 2 racks (8 GPUs across pooled nodes), expected baseline throughput ~40 concurrent sessions (estimate ~150k tokens/day)
   - Ramp: day 0 → keep 8 for first 30 days, then +8 at day 31 if utilization >70%
   - Burst: 8 additional spot/burst GPUs (best-effort, no SLA)
   - Pricing: monthly commit on GPU-hours in proposal PDF
2) Growth — "Committed scale"
   - Reserved: 16 x A100-40GB (min 16 GPUs reserved)
   - Initial config: 4 racks, baseline throughput ~90 concurrent sessions (~400k tokens/day)
   - Ramp: start 16 on day 0, +8 GPUs at day 30, +8 GPUs at day 60 → reach 32 by day 60
   - Burst: 16 GPUs available for autoscale (SLA-backed at stewardship tier)
   - Pricing: discounted commit rates (see cost workbook)
3) Enterprise — "High headroom"
   - Reserved: 32 x A100-40GB (min 32 GPUs reserved)
   - Initial config: 8 racks, baseline throughput ~180 concurrent sessions (~900k tokens/day)
   - Ramp: provision 32 at day 0, optional scale to 64 in 90 days for major rollouts
   - Burst: 32 GPUs immediate for high-availability/failover (SLA 99.9% uptime)
Operational notes / recommendations:
- Canary: roll the first model traffic through 2 GPUs (canary pool) with weighted routing and perf gates (qps, latency, error rate).
- KV prefix caching: enable to reduce repeated token generation for templated summaries. We estimate ~20–30% per-token cost reduction for repeated prompts.
- Quantization: we can ship an int8 variant for 70B to reduce VRAM and increase concurrency; tradeoffs documented in the PDF.
- Autoscaling: configure a floor = reserved GPUs, scale_up policy tied to 95th latency breach and queue depth. Rapid scale (burst) via dedicated burst pool (compatible with reserved metrics).
- Maintenance windows: monthly 2-hour maintenance; recommend scheduling in the 02:00–04:00 window local time.

I’ve attached: proposal-dedicated-reservation-v2.pdf and cost-breakdown-stellarhealth.xlsx.

Can we schedule a quick call with Rishi (SE) and Dev (Infra) tomorrow to walk the technical tradeoffs and finalize the ramp days?

Best,

Marissa / Dev —

Quick technical review and suggested edits (see attached inference-sizing-calcs.csv):
- Model memory: a 70B decoder at fp16 sits ~40GB usable; int8 moves us to ~28–30GB effective, leaving room for token KV caching. For 8 GPUs in Starter, peak concurrency will be tight if average session length and batch sizes are high. I recommend a min reserved of 12 GPUs for the Starter if they expect concurrent interactive usage >50 QPS-ish.
- Throughput estimates (per A100-40GB): ~350–500 tokens/sec with batching tuned for latency targets; with 16 GPUs expect ~5–8k tokens/sec aggregate.
- Latency: with batching and KV caching, interactive flows should be <350ms p95. Larger batch windows improve token/sec but increase tail latency; recommend dynamic batching window tied to SLA.
- Ramp logistics: auton provision lead time ~7 business days for reserved GPUs in us-east-1; OS/images + network + KMS onboarding ~3 business days parallel. For Apr 1 start we need PO by Mar 18 latest.
- Canary plan: seed 2 GPUs in the reserved pool for canary, progressively shift 10%→50%→100% traffic with automated rollback gates.

I attached a compact sizing calc and a template runbook skeleton. I’ll draft a 1-page SRE runbook that Marissa can attach to procurement.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
